sentences.en: So tell us about this case and, Adam, how it fits into all of that.
sentences.zh: 那么，请给我们介绍一下这个案件，亚当，以及它如何融入这一切。

sentences.en: Well, this case, Michael, presents probably the most fraught question of all, gender transition care for people under 18.
sentences.zh: 嗯，迈克尔，这个案件提出了可能是最令人不安的问题：18岁以下人群的性别肯定医疗护理。

sentences.en: And the case concerns a Tennessee law that bars providing some kinds of medical care to transgender minors, to people under 18 years of age.
sentences.zh: 该案涉及田纳西州的一项法律，该法律禁止向跨性别未成年人，即18岁以下的人提供某些医疗护理。

sentences.en: In particular, puberty blockers, hormone therapy, and surgery.
sentences.zh: 特别是青春期阻断剂、激素疗法和手术。

sentences.en: 23 other states have similar laws.
sentences.zh: 其他23个州也有类似的法律。

sentences.en: And the Tennessee law was challenged by three families and a doctor.
sentences.zh: 田纳西州的这项法律受到了三个家庭和一名医生的挑战。

sentences.en: The Biden administration intervened on the side of the families.
sentences.zh: 拜登政府介入并站在了这些家庭一边。

sentences.en: And they say that the law violates the Constitution's Equal Protection Clause.
sentences.zh: 他们认为该法律违反了宪法中的平等保护条款。

sentences.en: And can you just explain that argument started by these families and, as you said, picked up by the Biden administration about why this is an Equal Protection 14th Amendment case?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下这些家庭提出的，正如你所说，被拜登政府采纳的论点吗？为什么这是一个关于第14修正案平等保护的案件？

sentences.en: So the Equal Protection Clause says that some kinds of discrimination are presumptively unlawful.
sentences.zh: 平等保护条款规定，某些形式的歧视被推定为非法。

sentences.en: And the classic examples are, of course, race or gender.
sentences.zh: 经典的例子当然是种族或性别。

sentences.en: And what the families and the Biden administration say here is that this law is an example of sex discrimination.
sentences.zh: 这些家庭和拜登政府在这里所说的是，这项法律是性别歧视的一个例子。

sentences.en: It says that certain forms of care are available to everybody except minors who are seeking gender transition care.
sentences.zh: 它规定，除了寻求性别肯定护理的未成年人外，所有人都可以获得某些形式的护理。

sentences.en: And you have to take account of the sex of the child involved to know whether they're entitled to get that kind of treatment or not.
sentences.zh: 你必须考虑相关儿童的性别，才能知道他们是否有权获得那种治疗。

sentences.en: So think about it this way, Michael.
sentences.zh: 所以，迈克尔，换个角度想。

sentences.en: If you have a child assigned male at birth experiencing precocious puberty, meaning he's going through puberty earlier than he wants to, he can get puberty-blocking drugs.
sentences.zh: 如果一个出生时被指定为男性的孩子经历性早熟，也就是说他比预想的更早进入青春期，他可以获得青春期阻断药物。

sentences.en: If a transgender boy doesn't want to experience puberty because it doesn't align with his gender identity, he's not entitled to the very same treatment.
sentences.zh: 如果一个跨性别男孩不想经历青春期，因为它与他的性别认同不符，他就没有资格获得同样的治疗。

sentences.en: So the challengers would say that example tells you that this Tennessee law is a form of sex discrimination.
sentences.zh: 所以挑战者会说，这个例子告诉你，田纳西州的这项法律是一种性别歧视。

sentences.en: So under this Tennessee law, the same medicines and procedures are available or not available depending on whether you are a transgender boy or girl or not.
sentences.zh: 因此，根据田纳西州的这项法律，同样的药物和程序是否可用，取决于你是否是跨性别男孩或女孩。

sentences.en: And therefore, the claim being made is it's discriminating against trans boys and trans girls.
sentences.zh: 因此，所提出的主张是它歧视了跨性别男孩和女孩。

sentences.en: That's the claim under the 14th Amendment.
sentences.zh: 这就是第14修正案下的主张。

sentences.en: That's the challenger's argument.

sentences.en: The state will come back and say, no, we're not drawing distinctions based on transgender status.

sentences.en: These are different medical procedures, they would say.

sentences.en: And the reason why this matters is that the Supreme Court has said that if it is sex discrimination, the law is subject to a very demanding form of judicial scrutiny.
sentences.zh: 这件事之所以重要，是因为最高法院曾表示，如果是性别歧视，该法律将受到一种非常严格的司法审查。

sentences.en: Lawyers call it heightened scrutiny.
sentences.zh: 律师称之为高度审查。

sentences.en: And what it means is that a state has to prove that it has a good reason for the law and that the restriction advances that reason.
sentences.zh: 这意味着州政府必须证明其制定该法律有充分的理由，且该限制措施确实推进了这一理由。

sentences.en: And that's a difficult hurdle to overcome.

sentences.en: on transgender participation in sports.
sentences.zh: 关于跨性别者参与体育运动的影响。

sentences.en: Would transgender athletes have a constitutional right, as you see it, to play in women's and girls' sports, basketball, swimming, volleyball, track, et cetera, notwithstanding...
sentences.zh: 在你看来，跨性别运动员是否有宪法权利参加女子体育运动，篮球、游泳、排球、田径等，尽管……

sentences.en: And it wasn't just the conservative justices who seemed to want to expand the scope of their questioning beyond that narrow legal question.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是保守派大法官似乎想把提问范围扩大到那个狭窄的法律问题之外。

sentences.en: Some children suffer incredibly with gender dysphoria, don't they?
sentences.zh: 有些孩子因性别焦虑症而遭受难以置信的痛苦，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes, it's a very serious medical condition.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一种非常严重的医疗状况。

sentences.en: They think some attempt suicide?
sentences.zh: 他们认为有些人试图自杀？

sentences.en: Yes, the rates of suicide are striking, and it's a vulnerable...
sentences.zh: 是的，自杀率惊人，这是一个脆弱的……

sentences.en: Justice Sotomayor said that transgender minors suffering from gender dysphoria, the disconnect between sex assigned at birth and gender identity,
sentences.zh: 索托马约尔大法官说，患有性别焦虑症的跨性别未成年人，即出生时指定的性别与性别认同之间的脱节，

sentences.en: can go through very rough times, including potential suicide.
sentences.zh: 可能会经历非常艰难的时期，包括潜在的自杀。

sentences.en: One of the petitioners in this case described throwing up every day, going almost mute because of their inability to speak in a voice that they could live with.
sentences.zh: 本案的一名请愿者描述说每天呕吐，因为无法用自己能接受的声音说话而几乎变得哑口无言。

sentences.en: These are physically challenging situations as well, too.
sentences.zh: 这些也是身体上具有挑战性的情况。

sentences.en: So that this is an urgent situation, she says, that needs to be addressed and indicated that the Tennessee law gets in the way of what can be life-saving care.
sentences.zh: 所以她说，这是一个需要解决的紧急情况，并指出田纳西州的法律阻碍了可能挽救生命的护理。

sentences.en: On the other side of the balance...
sentences.zh: 在天平的另一端……

sentences.en: The restriction that I mentioned was imposed by the British government some months ago.
sentences.zh: 我提到的限制是英国政府几个月前实施的。

sentences.en: It was reaffirmed by the current labor...
sentences.zh: 它得到了现任工党的重申……

sentences.en: Justice Alito kind of surveyed the world and said that much of Europe has grown cautious about some forms of transgender care, to which the Solicitor General responded.
sentences.zh: 阿利托大法官审视了世界，说欧洲大部分地区对某些形式的跨性别护理变得谨慎，副总检察长对此做出了回应。

sentences.en: If the court wants to go ahead and look at what's happening in Europe, the UK has not categorically banned this care.
sentences.zh: 如果法院想继续看看欧洲正在发生什么，英国并没有绝对禁止这种护理。

sentences.en: Sweden, Finland, and Norway, the other jurisdictions that my friends point to have not banned this care.
sentences.zh: 瑞典、芬兰和挪威，我朋友们指出的其他司法管辖区，也没有禁止这种护理。

sentences.en: And I think that's because of the recognition that this care can provide critical, sometimes life-saving benefits for individuals with severe gender dysphoria.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是因为人们认识到，这种护理可以为患有严重性别焦虑症的个人提供关键的，有时是挽救生命的益处。

sentences.en: That it's true that there have been adjustments in the UK, in Sweden, but none of them have a categorical rule like the one in Tennessee forbidding transgender care as such.
sentences.zh: 确实，英国和瑞典进行了一些调整，但他们都没有像田纳西州那样制定绝对禁止跨性别护理的规则。

sentences.en: So, at this point, the argument and the justices are sort of all over the map, quite literally.
sentences.zh: 所以，在这一点上，辩论和大法官们的观点可以说是完全没有交集，字面意义上的各说各话。

sentences.en: Trans kids in sports, laws in Europe, you know, all very important stuff, but really beyond the very specific question of, does this law discriminate on the basis of sex?
sentences.zh: 跨性别青少年参与体育运动、欧洲的法律，你知道，这些都很重要，但实际上已经超出了那个非常具体的问题，即：这项法律是否基于性别进行歧视？

sentences.en: I guess, I think there might be some confusion a little bit, at least I'm confused because there's so many lines that this statute could draw.
sentences.zh: 我想，我觉得可能存在一点困惑，至少我很困惑，因为这项法规可能划定的界限实在太多了。

sentences.en: And then there was a striking moment when Justice Ketanji Brown-Jackson says, wait a second, we have a job here.
sentences.zh: 然后出现了一个引人注目的时刻，凯坦吉·布朗-杰克逊大法官说，等一下，我们在这里是有职责的。

sentences.en: It's not to decide the risks or benefits of the policies that justify the law.
sentences.zh: 我们的职责不是去裁定那些为法律辩护的政策所带来的风险或收益。

sentences.en: It's our job under the Constitution to decide, at least in the first instance, whether the law triggers the Equal Protection Clause.
sentences.zh: 根据宪法，我们的职责是，至少在第一审级上，判定该法律是否触发了平等保护条款。

sentences.en: And the question for equal protection purposes is, if you're right that there is a sex-based line being drawn, then, to the extent the plaintiffs are implicated by that line,
sentences.zh: 而平等保护目的下的问题是，如果你认为确实划定了一条基于性别的界限，那么，在原告受到该界限影响的范围内，

sentences.en: don't we have to apply heightened scrutiny in evaluating their claims?
sentences.zh: 我们在评估他们的诉求时，难道不应该适用更严格的审查标准吗？

sentences.en: Yes, that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: She said that's the job of the Supreme Court, to police the 14th Amendment and at least reach the initial question of, is this sex discrimination?
sentences.zh: 她说，最高法院的职责就是监督第十四修正案，并至少要解决最初的问题：这是否属于性别歧视？

sentences.en: And does that mean that a heightened form of judicial review kicks in?
sentences.zh: 这是否意味着一种更严格的司法审查形式将会启动？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: She's sort of like, people, focus.
sentences.zh: 她就像是在说，各位，请集中注意力。

sentences.en: We have a job here.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里是有职责的。

sentences.en: It was a striking moment.
sentences.zh: 那是一个引人注目的时刻。

sentences.en: Mr. Strangio?
sentences.zh: 斯特兰吉奥先生？

sentences.en: Mr. Chief Justice, and may it please the court.
sentences.zh: 首席大法官先生，法庭请允许我发言。

sentences.en: But I think in a lot of ways, one of the most memorable moments in the arguments came when another lawyer challenging the law stood up to argue.
sentences.zh: 但我认为在很多方面，辩论中最令人难忘的时刻之一，是另一位挑战该法律的律师站起来辩论时。

sentences.en: But SB1 has taken away the only treatment that relieved years of suffering for each of the adolescent plaintiffs.
sentences.zh: 但SB1法案剥夺了每一位青少年原告多年来赖以缓解痛苦的唯一治疗方法。

sentences.en: Chase Strangio, a lawyer with the ACLU, representing the families and the doctor challenging the law, is the first transgender lawyer ever to argue before the Supreme Court,
sentences.zh: 蔡斯·斯特兰吉奥，美国公民自由联盟（ACLU）的一名律师，代表那些家庭和挑战该法律的医生，他是第一位在最高法院进行辩论的跨性别律师，

sentences.en: or at least the first openly transgender lawyer.
sentences.zh: 或者至少是第一位公开身份的跨性别律师。

sentences.en: Let me ask a question about another issue that came up during Justice Kagan's questioning.
sentences.zh: 让我问一个关于卡根大法官提问期间出现的另一个问题。

sentences.en: And he pretty quickly gets into an exchange with Justice Alito, who's one of the court's most conservative members, that's really quite remarkable.
sentences.zh: 他很快就与阿利托大法官——法院最保守的成员之一——展开了一场非常引人注目的交锋。

sentences.en: Is transgender status immutable?
sentences.zh: 跨性别身份是不可改变的吗？

sentences.en: Alito asks him whether transgender identity is immutable.
sentences.zh: 阿利托问他跨性别身份是否是不可改变的。

sentences.en: I think that the record shows that the discordance between a person's birth, sex, and gender identity has a strong biological basis and would satisfy an immutability teSt.
sentences.zh: 我认为记录显示，一个人的出生性别与性别认同之间的不一致有很强的生物学基础，并且符合不可改变性的测试。

sentences.en: And Alito is essentially asking a transgender person, a lawyer arguing before the court, is your identity an essential element of who you are?
sentences.zh: 而阿利托本质上是在问一位跨性别者，一位在法庭上辩论的律师：你的身份是你本质的一部分吗？

sentences.en: And it's not just a striking moment.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是一个引人注目的时刻。

sentences.en: It also has some legal significance.
sentences.zh: 它还具有一定的法律意义。

sentences.en: Whether or not a characteristic is immutable plays into deciding whether that characteristic can make you into a protected class.
sentences.zh: 一个特征是否不可改变，对于决定该特征是否能使你成为受保护群体的一部分至关重要。

sentences.en: So this was not only personal, but also an important point for his side to try to win.
sentences.zh: 所以这不仅是个人的，对于他这一方试图胜诉来说，也是一个重要的论点。

sentences.en: If Tennessee can have an end run around heightened scrutiny by asserting at the outset that biology justifies the sex-based differential in the law,
sentences.zh: 如果田纳西州可以通过在起初断言生物学证明了法律中基于性别的差异是正当的，从而绕过更严格的审查，

sentences.en: that would undermine decades of this court's precedent.
sentences.zh: 那将破坏本法院几十年的先例。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you, counsel.
sentences.zh: 谢谢，律师。

sentences.en: So, Adam, when the two lawyers arguing against this Tennessee law are done and about to hand it over to the folks defending this law, what are you thinking?
sentences.zh: 那么，亚当，当反对这项田纳西州法律的两位律师辩论结束，即将交给为该法律辩护的人时，你在想什么？

sentences.en: So, Michael, by the time the challengers finished, and it was kind of an unwieldy romp through a lot of different areas,
sentences.zh: 那么，迈克尔，当挑战者们结束辩论时，那过程就像是在许多不同领域中漫无目的地穿梭，

sentences.en: not tightly focused on the legal question before the justices, I kind of had the sense that the challengers were facing an uphill fight in what they had to prove
sentences.zh: 并没有紧扣大法官们面前的法律问题，我当时有一种感觉，挑战者们在证明这一点时面临着一场艰苦的战斗，

sentences.en: and persuading the more conservative majority that this law amounts to sex discrimination.
sentences.zh: 并且要说服更保守的多数派相信这项法律等同于性别歧视。

sentences.en: And that was before we even heard from Tennessee's lawyer who was defending the law and saying that it wasn't about sex discrimination, but about something else entirely.
sentences.zh: 而那还是在我们听取田纳西州律师的辩护之前，他为该法律辩护并称这根本不是关于性别歧视，而是完全关于其他事情。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我编写了《Connections》游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏中的谜题之一，我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog, and I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗，我也喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由人制作的，就像你们刚才听到的那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 即可开始游戏。

sentences.en: So, Adam, tell us about the second half of these arguments when the lawyer for Tennessee argues his side of this case.
sentences.zh: 那么，亚当，告诉我们这些辩论的后半部分，当田纳西州的律师为他的立场进行辩论时的情况。

sentences.en: Mr. Rice?
sentences.zh: 赖斯先生？

sentences.en: Mr. Chief Justice, and may it please the court.
sentences.zh: 首席大法官先生，法庭请允许我发言。

sentences.en: Tennessee's Solicitor General,
sentences.zh: 田纳西州副总检察长，

sentences.en: Matthew Rice, says the other side misunderstands what's going on here.
sentences.zh: 马修·赖斯，说对方误解了这里发生的事情。

sentences.en: The law imposes an across-the-board rule that allows the use of drugs and surgeries for some medical purposes, but not for others.
sentences.zh: 该法律实施了一项全面规则，允许将药物和手术用于某些医疗目的，但不允许用于其他目的。

sentences.en: Its application turns entirely on medical purpose, not a patient's sex.
sentences.zh: 其适用完全取决于医疗目的，而不是患者的性别。

sentences.en: That is not sex discrimination.
sentences.zh: 那不是性别歧视。

sentences.en: That this isn't sex discrimination.
sentences.zh: 这并不是性别歧视。

sentences.en: Neither boys nor girls can get this kind of medical treatment.
sentences.zh: 无论男孩还是女孩都无法获得这种医疗。

sentences.en: He says it's a restriction on medical procedures.
sentences.zh: 他说这是对医疗程序的限制。

sentences.en: It's a restriction on the purpose of the procedure, not on any particular gender, not on any particular sex of a patient.
sentences.zh: 这是对程序目的的限制，而不是针对任何特定的性别，也不是针对患者的任何特定性别。

sentences.en: The Equal Protection Clause does not require the states to blind themselves to medical reality or to treat unlike things the same.
sentences.zh: 平等保护条款并不要求各州对医疗现实视而不见，也不要求它们对不同的事物一视同仁。

sentences.en: He's saying this law, if it discriminates against anyone, does so based on the purpose of this medical treatment.
sentences.zh: 他是在说，如果这项法律歧视任何人，那也是基于这种医疗的目的。

sentences.en: If the purpose is to transition a minor, we're not for it.
sentences.zh: 如果目的是为了让未成年人进行性别转换，我们就不支持。

sentences.en: If it's for something else, we are.
sentences.zh: 如果是为了其他目的，我们就支持。

sentences.en: He's saying as a result, it cannot be construed as discriminatory based on sex.
sentences.zh: 他是在说，因此，这不能被解释为基于性别的歧视。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He would also say, listen, we are discriminating based on age, but we're allowed to do that.
sentences.zh: 他还会说，听着，我们确实是基于年龄进行歧视，但我们被允许这样做。

sentences.en: We are discriminating based on, as you say, Michael, what the medical procedures are, but we're not discriminating, he claims, based on the gender of the patient.
sentences.zh: 我们确实是基于你所说的医疗程序进行歧视，迈克尔，但他声称，我们并不是基于患者的性别进行歧视。

sentences.en: And what do the justices say to that?
sentences.zh: 大法官们对此怎么说？

sentences.en: Both the SG and petitioner have suggested...
sentences.zh: 副总检察长和请愿人都建议……

sentences.en: Justice Clarence Thomas asks the first question to Rice, saying that maybe Tennessee could have taken a different approach to its law.
sentences.zh: 克拉伦斯·托马斯大法官向赖斯提出了第一个问题，说也许田纳西州本可以采取不同的方式来制定法律。

sentences.en: So it becomes a pure exercise of weighing benefits versus risk.
sentences.zh: 所以这变成了一个纯粹权衡利益与风险的练习。

sentences.en: And the question of how many...
sentences.zh: 而关于多少……的问题

sentences.en: And Rice starts to answer the question, says, you know, there are risks to this kind of intervention.
sentences.zh: 赖斯开始回答这个问题，说，你知道，这种干预是有风险的。

sentences.en: I'm sorry, counselor.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，律师。

sentences.en: Every medical treatment has a risk.
sentences.zh: 每种医疗都有风险。

sentences.en: Even taking aspirin.
sentences.zh: 即使是服用阿司匹林。

sentences.en: And as he's answering,
sentences.zh: 就在他回答时，

sentences.en: Justice Sotomayor interrupts him and says, wait a second, all kinds of medical procedures have risks.
sentences.zh: 索托马约尔大法官打断了他，说，等一下，各种医疗程序都有风险。

sentences.en: There is always going to be a percentage of the population under any medical treatment that's going to suffer a harm.
sentences.zh: 在任何医疗手段下，总会有一定比例的人群会受到伤害。

sentences.en: So the question in my mind is not,
sentences.zh: 所以在我看来，问题不在于，

sentences.en: do policymakers decide whether one person's life is more valuable?
sentences.zh: 决策者是否决定一个人的生命比另一个人的更有价值？

sentences.en: But the question is, what are you trying to achieve and what's the countervailing value of the harm that comes to transgender youths who are deeply distressed
sentences.zh: 而问题在于，你试图实现什么，以及对于那些深受困扰的跨性别青少年来说，这种伤害的抵消价值是什么，

sentences.en: by the disconnect between their gender assigned at birth and their current gender identity?
sentences.zh: 他们因出生时指定的性别与当前的性别认同之间的脱节而感到痛苦？

sentences.en: But the other is...
sentences.zh: 但另一个是……

sentences.en: Can you stop one sex from the other, one person of one sex from another sex, from receiving that benefit?
sentences.zh: 你能阻止一个性别的人，一个特定性别的人，从获得那种利益吗？

sentences.en: That the same medical treatment under this law is unavailable to transgender kids, but available to other kids.
sentences.zh: 即根据这项法律，同样的医疗在跨性别儿童身上无法获得，但在其他孩子身上却可以。

sentences.en: That's the sex-based difference.
sentences.zh: 这就是基于性别的差异。

sentences.en: It's not the...
sentences.zh: 这不是……

sentences.en: The medical condition is the same.
sentences.zh: 医疗状况是一样的。

sentences.en: We don't agree.
sentences.zh: 我们不同意。

sentences.en: But you're saying one sex is getting it and the other's not.
sentences.zh: 但你是在说一个性别的人能得到，而另一个不能。

sentences.en: We do not agree that the medical...
sentences.zh: 我们不同意医疗……

sentences.en: And the other liberal justices sort of pile on.
sentences.zh: 其他自由派大法官也纷纷加入。

sentences.en: They're loaded for bear.
sentences.zh: 他们做好了充分的准备。

sentences.en: Now, looking at this statute, a girl comes in biologically and asks for a hormone to deepen her voice in order to affirm the identity that she chooses, which is masculinity.
sentences.zh: 现在，看看这项法规，一个女孩在生理上走进来，要求使用激素来加深她的声音，以确认她选择的身份，即男性化。

sentences.en: Justice Jackson presses the lawyer on the distinction between two different minors seeking the same treatment, testosterone to lower their voices.
sentences.zh: 杰克逊大法官向律师追问两个寻求相同治疗的未成年人之间的区别，即使用睾酮来降低他们的声音。

sentences.en: She wants to...
sentences.zh: 她想……

sentences.en: I'm sorry, one more time, Your Honor.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，请再说一遍，法官阁下。

sentences.en: She wants to get the medication in order to deepen her voice and affirm her masculinity.
sentences.zh: 她想获得药物以加深她的声音并确认她的男性化身份。

sentences.en: Your Honor, I think if it's for the purpose of identifying inconsistent with their sex, she would be barred from doing that under the...
sentences.zh: 法官阁下，我认为如果是为了认同与他们性别不一致的目的，根据……她将被禁止这样做。

sentences.en: But isn't that the point, Mr. Rice, that...
sentences.zh: 但赖斯先生，这难道不是重点吗，即……

sentences.en: And Justice Kagan jumps in as well.
